flawed_step: The claimed transitivity of the probability comparison is false.
counterexample: Let Y=0 almost surely. Independently, let X=1 with probability 0.6 and X=-2 with probability 0.4; let Z=-1 with probability 0.6 and Z=2 with probability 0.4. Then P(X>Y)=0.6>1/2 and P(Y>Z)=0.6>1/2. However, X>Z occurs only when X=1 and Z=-1, so P(X>Z)=0.6*0.6=0.36<=1/2.
assessment_summary: These mutually independent real-valued random variables satisfy both hypotheses but violate the conclusion, so the relation is not transitive.
